segments.text: Euclid's Elements, Book One, Proposition Thirty-One. Construct through a given point a line parallel to a given line. Let A be the given point, and segment B C the given line. We construct through point A a line parallel to segment B C.

subsegments.text: Euclid's Elements, Book One, Proposition Thirty-One. Construct through a given point a line parallel to a given line. Let A be the given point, and segment B C the given line. We construct through point A a line parallel to segment B C.

segments.style: speaking briskly, nimble, crisp, and composed
segments.text: Take a point D at random on segment B C, and construct segment A D. By Proposition Twenty-Three, on segment D A and at point A on it, construct angle D A E equal to angle A D C. Then extend segment E A in a straight line to A F.

segments.style: speaking briskly, nimble, crisp, and composed
segments.text: Since transversal A D falling on segments B C and E F makes the alternate interior angles D A E and A D C equal, by Proposition Twenty-Seven, segment E F is parallel to segment B C. Therefore through the given point A, line E A F has been constructed parallel to the given line B C, as was required to do.
